summary: Metric aliasing during route rename causes alert notifications to be delivered to incorrect owners
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report alert notifications being sent to the wrong on-call contact after they rename a route/alias in the Console. Impact: missed or misrouted alerts for several teams at FinSecure Analytics (enterprise) causing delayed incident response.

Impact:
- ~3 alert notifications over 24h window routed to deprecated team emails for the customer.
- Alert thumbnails in Slack linked to new route IDs but notification recipients reflect pre-rename alias mapping.

Environment:
- Production Console (us-east)
- Affected tenant: FinSecure Analytics (enterprise org id redacted)

Observed behaviour appears correlated with a recent route alias rename and a retention compaction window that evicted legacy alias mappings before downstream alert routing tables were updated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In Console, create route R1 with alias 'payments-ingest-prod' and assign alert policy A -> notify team payments-team@finsecure.com
2) Trigger a synthetic spike that fires alert policy A and confirm notification delivered to payments-team@finsecure.com
3) Rename route alias to 'payments-ingest-main' (route id unchanged), and update alert policy display name to match new alias
4) Wait for retention compaction (customer reports ~6h window) or force metadata backfill, then trigger synthetic spike again
5) Observe that alert notifications are delivered to payments-team-old@finsecure.com (legacy address) while Console UI shows the new alias and new policy bindings
logs_excerpt:
[2026-03-12T08:42:13Z] ALERT_DISPATCH route_id=rt-0a1b alias=payments-ingest-main resolved_alias_mapping=payments-ingest-prod recipient=payments-team-old@finsecure.com dispatch_status=sent
[2026-03-12T08:42:13Z] UI_EVENT route_id=rt-0a1b alias=payments-ingest-main policy=A notification_preview=payments-team@finsecure.com
(Dispatch log indicates resolver used stale alias-to-recipient mapping cached in alert-routing service.)
comments: 2026-03-12 09:05 - Support - Aisha Patel: Customer submitted with screenshots. They changed route alias yesterday evening; started seeing misrouted alerts this morning. Attached Slack thread #support-finsecure.

2026-03-12 10:20 - Oncall SRE - Marcus Grant: Started triage. Initial hypothesis: alias rename didn't invalidate alert-routing cache. Requested full dispatch logs and alias-change audit trail. Filed INT-834 for internal metadata reconciliation check.

2026-03-12 11:04 - Customer - Jenna Liu (FinSecure): We confirmed three alerts went to payments-team-old@finsecure.com between 07:40-09:10. The UI shows the policy pointing at payments-team@finsecure.com. We rely on email recipients for pager escalation.

2026-03-12 13:18 - Support - Marcus Grant: Found gap: retention compaction job removed legacy alias entries from the alias_index shard before alert-routing service consumed CDC stream for metadata update. Routing service fell back to an older in-memory map that still referenced the deprecated contact. See logs in github.com/redwood/usage-ingest/pull/2087 for CDC ordering race reproduction.

2026-03-13 08:40 - Engineering - Priya Kapoor: Pushed hotfix to ensure alias-change events are applied transactionally with routing table updates (PR #4123). Rolling to us-east staging now. Will coordinate a backfill for affected tenant mapping reconciliation.
investigation_notes: Timeline: alias rename occurred 2026-03-11 21:12, retention compaction for alias_index shard executed 2026-03-12 02:00. CDC stream consumer lagged ~3.5h due to transient kinesis throttling (see Kinesis metrics). Result: dispatch service attempted to resolve alias after compaction but before consumer applied rename event, so it matched by deprecated alias->recipient mapping persisted in old in-memory structure. Root cause combination: 1) compaction TTL shorter than guaranteed event-consumption window, 2) routing consumer does not persist checkpoints atomically with compaction markers, 3) no defensive lookup fallback to authoritative metadata service when in-memory map misses present alias. Reproducible in local harness by simulating consumer lag and compaction. Related internal follow-ups: INT-834 (consumer checkpointing), INT-907 (compaction TTL review).
workaround:
1) Temporary mitigation: disable aggressive alias_index compaction for affected orgs (feature flag) until backfill completes.
2) Customer can re-apply the alert policy binding (open and save) which forces a routing-table write and immediate re-publish to dispatch queue (not ideal at scale).
resolution: Engineering merged hotfix PR to make alias-change application transactional with routing table update and to add a fallback authoritative metadata fetch when dispatch returns an unexpected recipient. Hotfix rolled to us-east 2026-03-13 02:10 UTC. Backfill job ran against FinSecure org at 2026-03-13 05:20 and reconciled 100% of affected alias mappings. Customer confirmed no further misrouted alerts after reconciliation. Follow-up: increase compaction safety window and add monitoring on alias-index consumer lag (see INT-907).
notes_next_steps:
- Close SUP after customer confirmation for 48h without regression.
- INT-834 to ensure CDC consumers checkpoint atomically; target ETA 2026-03-20.
- INT-907 to review compaction TTLs and safety window; target ETA 2026-03-24.
- Add automated test in CI to simulate compaction+consumer-lag and ensure dispatch service uses authoritative lookup if in-memory state missing.
